title: Microsoft Azure Reference
description: A quick reminder of the ideas and examples in the Microsoft Azure lessons. Open the linked lesson when you need more help.

entries.name: Meet the Azure cloud
entries.summary: Microsoft Azure offers rented services for computing, storage and networking. A useful design begins with the job, not with the longest list of services.

example.code:
Goal: publish a small static club page
Inputs: HTML, CSS and image files
Decision: choose a static-file hosting option

notes: Creating real cloud resources can incur charges; these lessons only describe them.

entries.name: Subscriptions and resource groups
entries.summary: An Azure subscription is a billing and management boundary. A resource group collects related resources for a project.

example.code:
Subscription: approved learning subscription
Resource group: rg-club-practice
Resources: storage and monitoring for the club project

notes: Deleting a resource group deletes its contained resources; never do that to an unknown group.

entries.name: Regions and availability
entries.summary: An Azure region is a geographic area. Many regions offer availability zones, which provide separate physical locations within the region.

example.code:
Choose a supported region
Check whether the chosen service supports zones there
Plan copies if the availability need justifies them

notes: Check the service's current regional support before planning a zonal feature.

entries.name: Microsoft Entra identities
entries.summary: Microsoft Entra ID manages identities. An identity can represent a person, application or workload, depending on how access is arranged.

example.code:
Person identity: a reviewer
Workload identity: an approved application
Access decision: assign only the required role at the right scope

notes: Do not share one personal account among many learners.

entries.name: Azure role assignments
entries.summary: Azure role-based access control assigns a role to an identity at a scope. Scope can be a resource, resource group or broader boundary.

example.code:
Identity: fictional reviewer
Role: Reader
Scope: rg-club-practice

notes: A broad scope can grant more access than intended.

entries.name: Blob Storage containers
entries.summary: Azure Blob Storage keeps objects called blobs. Containers group blobs inside a storage account.

example.code:
Storage account -> container club-files
Container -> blob images/logo.png

notes: Public read access should be an explicit decision, not a fix for every permission error.

entries.name: Static website files
entries.summary: An Azure Storage static website uses an index document and an error document. It is a way to serve files, not an application backend.

example.code:
Index document: index.html
Error document: 404.html
Content: compiled frontend files

notes: Static website access has different settings from ordinary private blob access; check the official service guide.

entries.name: Virtual machines need upkeep
entries.summary: An Azure virtual machine is a configurable computer in the cloud. Its operating system and software still need care.

example.code:
Planned VM: one Linux practice machine
Owner tasks: updates, accounts, disk care and monitoring

notes: Deleting or stopping one resource may leave related disks or addresses with their own costs.

entries.name: Virtual networks and subnets
entries.summary: A virtual network provides a private network space. Subnets divide that space into smaller address ranges for resources.
notes: Do not confuse an address range with a permission to access a service.

entries.name: Network security groups
entries.summary: A network security group contains rules that allow or deny network traffic. Rules have priorities, so their order matters.

example.code:
Rule priority 100: allow approved HTTPS traffic
Later rules: handle other traffic according to the plan

notes: Do not open every port to the internet to make troubleshooting easier.

entries.name: Azure Monitor helps you observe
entries.summary: Azure Monitor collects supported metrics and logs. Alerts can tell you when a chosen condition is met.

example.code:
Metric: failed requests
Alert: more failures than the agreed threshold
Investigation: compare logs and recent changes

notes: Collect only the information needed for the task, especially on sites used by children.

entries.name: Cost planning and cleanup
entries.summary: Azure budgets can notify you about spending. Review actual resource costs and plan cleanup; notifications are not a general guarantee that spending stops.

example.code:
Fictional budget: 10 units
Alert at 80 percent: 8 units
Cleanup list: only resources created for this approved practice

notes: Never delete a shared resource group as casual cleanup.
